title: Valid Palindrome
statement: A phrase is a **palindrome** if, after ignoring everything that is not a letter or digit and ignoring upper/lower case, it reads the same forwards and backwards. Given a string `s`, return `True` if it is a palindrome.

example.why: Keeping only letters and lowering them gives "atoyota", which reads the same both ways.

more.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"

idea: A palindrome's first character equals its last, its second equals its second-to-last, and so on.
So put one pointer at each end and compare the two characters, moving both inward after every match.
Spaces and punctuation do not count: whenever a pointer lands on one, just step over it. Compare letters in lower case.

complexity.timeWhy: Each pointer only moves inward, so every character is looked at once.
complexity.spaceWhy: Just two pointers — no cleaned-up copy of the string is built.

steps.text: Our example: **`s = "A Toyota!"`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
Put `left` on the first character and `right` on the last. We compare them pair by pair, moving inward.
`"!"` is not a letter or digit, so it does not count. Step `right` over it.
Compare `A` with `a`, ignoring case: `a` equals `a` — this pair **matches**.
The pair matched, so move both pointers one step inward.
`" "` is not a letter or digit, so it does not count. Step `left` over it.
Compare `T` with `t`, ignoring case: `t` equals `t` — this pair **matches**.
The pair matched, so move both pointers one step inward.
Compare `o` with `o`, ignoring case: `o` equals `o` — this pair **matches**.
The pair matched, so move both pointers one step inward.
The pointers have met in the middle. Every pair matched.
No mismatch was found, so the phrase is a palindrome → **True**.
Done — the answer is **`True`**. Keeping only letters and lowering them gives "atoyota", which reads the same both ways.
